input.efficiencyHint: Guide values: drop hammer 0.75 · hydraulic 0.9 · diesel 0.8 · steam/air 0.75. Use the supplier's figure if available.
input.pileHint: Precast concrete 350×350 mm: A = 0.1225 m², E ≈ 30 GPa, approx. 294 kg/m. Steel: E = 210 GPa.
input.pasteHint: You can paste from a spreadsheet: two columns (depth, blows), one interval per row.
input.requiredHint: The load the pile has to carry (characteristic). Each formula divides its ultimate resistance by its own factor of safety.
input.advanced: Factors of safety and Hiley parameters
input.hileyHint: c = c1 + c2 + c3: helmet, pile and soil combined; for concrete on a timber cushion usually 6 to 12 mm. e: 0.25 (softwood) to 0.5 (steel on steel).

visual.empty: Fill in the pile driving record to show the chart.
visual.aria: Pile driving record and allowable load per pile driving formula against depth

sheet.title: Driving record assessment
sheet.pile: Weight of pile and helmet P
sheet.reliableNote: Grey: formulas with a large scatter compared with load tests; they do not count towards the verdict.
sheet.failText: The driving record is not satisfactory
sheet.verdictLine: Allowable {{allow}} kN (median of {{names}}) against required {{req}} kN: u.c. {{uc}}
sheet.m1: A pile driving formula estimates the resistance during driving from the energy per blow and the set per blow. It is a check on the execution; the bearing capacity follows from the CPTs in accordance with NEN 9997-1.
sheet.m2: Comparisons with load tests (Flaate 1964, Olson and Flaate 1967, FHWA) show the smallest scatter for Janbu, the Danish formula, Hiley and Gates. The Dutch and Engineering News formulas scatter widely; hence their high factor of safety.
sheet.m3: In clay and fine sand the resistance changes after driving (set-up or relaxation). In that case also assess a restrike after a few days.
sheet.m4: With a set per blow smaller than 2 mm or larger than 50 mm the formulas are unreliable.
sheet.m5: Gates uses the nominal energy W·h without efficiency; the other formulas use η·W·h.

errors.hammer: Enter the mass and the drop height of the pile hammer.
errors.restitution: The coefficient of restitution lies between 0 and 1.
errors.pile: Enter the mass, length, cross-section and modulus of elasticity of the pile.
errors.tocht: The interval length must be greater than 0.
errors.negative: Helmet mass and temporary compression must not be negative.
errors.noRows: Fill in the pile driving record: the depth and the number of blows per interval.
errors.blows: Each interval has at least one blow.
errors.required: Enter the required load on the pile.
errors.noFormula: Select at least one pile driving formula.

warn.refusal: Set per blow {{set}} mm (< 2 mm): the pile is practically at refusal. Pile driving formulas are unreliable here and continued driving may damage the pile.
warn.easy: Set per blow {{set}} mm (> 50 mm): very easy driving; the formulas then readily overestimate the bearing capacity.
warn.lightHammer: The hammer weighs less than half of the pile and helmet (W/P = {{ratio}}): much of the blow energy is lost in the impact.
warn.noReliable: None of the more reliable formulas (Hiley, Janbu, Danish, Gates) has been selected; the verdict rests on formulas with a large scatter.
warn.spread: The formulas differ by more than a factor of 3. Use the result as a check on the execution, not as a bearing capacity.
warn.decreasing: The number of blows per interval decreases over the last intervals: the pile toe may be leaving the bearing layer, or relaxation is occurring.
